chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:
"Zakat is due on silent wealth upon which the year has passed and which has not been moved (i.e., not spent or circulated)."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Zakat on stored wealth that is not actively traded?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the specific condition of 'Hawl' (lunar year) for 'Mal al-Samit' (static wealth like stored gold or inventory), distinguishing it from active trade capital. In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith is foundational for determining the timing of Zakat liability on savings and assets that remain untouched, emphasizing that mere possession over a complete year triggers the obligation. It underscores the principle that Zakat is a purification of accumulated wealth, requiring the full cycle of time to pass without the owner actively circulating or spending the funds.
